classification.bridgeTileFrames: Observed: right-to-left removal, about four native frames per 16px tile; sampled complete collapse spans 52 to 60 frames.
classification.bowserGravityAndMaxFall: Fitted: 0.0625 and 2.25 fit all eight falling bodies with max 1px residual, allowing the onset/subpixel interval left unresolved by 7/8-frame images.
classification.walkAndBraking: Fitted: shared 1.5 speed, separation48, deceleration0.037109375, unquantized cutscene integration. 118 positions across eight castles have max1px residual with a fitted initial subpixel fraction.
classification.camera: Observed independently from static ledge and NPC registration: scrolling continues at1.5 after Mario brakes, until the explicit observed final view. The1px final-view differences are measured geometry, not timing offsets.
classification.collapseInitialWaitFrames: Inferred central candidate. Contact-to-first-removal screenshots admit roughly0..37 frames across eight traces; the inherited timer phase is unresolved.16 is not a measured exact constant.
classification.bowserReleaseFeetYAndReleaseFallSpeed: Inferred geometric release candidate: hold Mario while Bowser falls, then resume ordinary vertical collision at boss feet264. Independently extrapolated camera starts correspond to feet about262..274, so this central geometric threshold leaves roughly3frames of phase error. Four-pixel initial player fall is consistent with the first ledge samples; horizontal movement while settling uses ordinary walking acceleration.
classification.messageTiming: Second line128 fits every sampled interval.368-frame hold is a central candidate: first THANK to first visible next-intro samples span368..383; display erasure and inherited phase prevent a single verified2-frame transition fit.
classification.ending: Observed:8-4 terminal occurs on the camera-completion image, before any dialogue. Post-terminal THANK/quest text timing is unavailable; existing later text is an explicitly inferred presentation. No arbitrary NPC-arrival wait controls victory.
